answers.answer: Shuffle all 4 Conflict III cards and place them on the bottom; shuffle all 9 II cards and deal 5 above them; shuffle all 3 I cards and deal 1 on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: 10-card Conflict Deck; return unused cards unseen.

answers.answer: In four players, a human starts at 1 VP; in other player counts including three, at 0 VP. Each starts with two Agents on the Leader and a third Swordmaster Agent beside the board; three troops in their garrison and nine in supply; and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: score 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; two Agents; third beside board; three troops in garrison, nine in supply; take 1 water.

answers.answer: You may Reveal while Agents remain, but after Revealing your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot later take an Agent turn that round. Reveal effects come only from the cards just revealed from your remaining hand, not Agent-turn cards. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Reveal Turn: Agent turns optional; once Revealed, turns skipped; resolve revealed cards only; Clean Up all cards.

answers.answer: Resources from a Plot Intrigue played before placing your Agent can pay the entry cost if gained before entry. Resources from the card being played to send the Agent or from the destination itself cannot pay that same entry cost; entry is paid before those effects. One card sends only one Agent using one Agent icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn and may only be revealed.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: Plot before placement may grant entry resources; later gains cannot pay that entry. Agent Turn: choose only one icon; no icons means Reveal only.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy all three troops recruited that turn plus up to two of the four already in your garrison: at most five troops. At a non-Combat space, the troops recruited go into your garrison and cannot be deployed there. Recruited troops come from your supply; if it is empty you cannot recruit more until troops return to it.
answers.evidence: Recruiting & Deploying: recruited this turn plus up to two from garrison at Combat spaces; recruit from supply; garrison units do not help Combats.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any space connected to an observation post where you currently have a Spy; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls your Spy from a connected post to bypass another player's Agent at the destination, not your own Agent. Gather Intelligence recalls a Spy from a connected post to draw a card, chosen just after placing your Agent and before space/card effects. The same Spy cannot pay for both Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, though different Spies may do each on one placement.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Spy Agent icon does not recall; Infiltrate bypasses another player; Gather timing; cannot recall same Spy for both.

answers.answer: Strength is 2 troops × 2, plus 1 sandworm × 3, plus 4 revealed swords × 1 = 11. If your final unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. A player with no unit in the Conflict has strength 0 and cannot play Combat Intrigue because only players with at least one unit may do so.
answers.evidence: Strength: troop 2, sandworm 3, sword 1; no units means strength 0. Combat Intrigue requires at least one unit.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing once does not prevent you from playing later; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply (not garrison), sandworms return to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: may play after earlier pass; resolve once all involved pass consecutively. Cleanup returns troops to supply, worms to bank, markers to 0.

answers.answer: With two tied for first in four-player play, each gets the second reward; the remaining players compete for the third reward, and nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. With the same tie in a three-player game, each tied player gets the second reward, no other reward is given, and nobody takes the card. A player with 0 strength receives no reward.
answers.evidence: Combat ties by player count; Resolve Combat: zero strength receives no reward.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards; two sandworms do not quadruple them. Control of a location and battle icons on a won Conflict card cannot be doubled. If the reward lets you pay 3 spice for 1 VP, you may pay 3 spice a second time to gain the VP a second time (6 spice for 2 VP total).
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling: one or more doubles; location control and battle icons excluded; may pay optional cost again.

answers.answer: After winning and taking a Conflict card face up into your supply, check it for a matching battle icon against another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. If a match exists, you must flip the pair face down and gain 1 VP. During Endgame, a wild icon can match any one of the three icon types in your supply, for 1 VP when the pair is flipped.
answers.evidence: Winner takes Conflict card face up, then mandatory match check; Battle Icons section lists face-up cards and wild Endgame match.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; dropping below 2 loses it and reaching 2 again regains it. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is retained below 4 and earned again on returning to 4; the first player to 4 also gets the Alliance token and its 1 VP, which is tied to holding it. Tying the holder does not take the Alliance; a challenger must rise above the holder.
answers.evidence: Victory Points—Faction Influence: 2 and 4 rewards/reversal; tying does not steal; rising above transfers.

answers.answer: During Reveal you may spend gained Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool Persuasion from sources to buy one card and split one source across cards. The Imperium Row is replenished to five cards, so you can buy the replacement immediately if able. Acquired cards go face up to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards: timing, pooling/splitting, replacement, acquired card to discard.

answers.answer: At a Maker space with no Agent during Makers, add 1 spice to its bonus spot, accumulating with previous bonus spice; visiting gains all bonus spice there. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two sandworms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one sandworm. Sandworms cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin while the Shield Wall remains; removing it permits summoning to any Conflict. Hooks are only required when the effect specifies them and are retained, not spent. A worm is placed directly in the Conflict, never a garrison.
answers.evidence: Makers; Deep Desert/Hagga Basin board table; Sandworms and Shield Wall rules; FAQ says Hooks retained.

answers.answer: At Recall, if anyone has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty, Endgame is triggered. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigues, then most VP wins. Rulebook tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Scoring/Victory Conditions: Endgame timing, Endgame Intrigue, winner and tiebreak order.

answers.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contracts; expose 2 face up and put the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Add 4 additional Intrigue cards to that deck and 4 additional Imperium cards to that deck. Shaddam Corrino IV is an optional Leader choice, not compulsory. The 10 contrasting-back contracts are for Rise of Ix and are left in the box; standard CHOAM uses all 20 standard contracts.
answers.evidence: CHOAM setup changes and contrasting-back contracts note.

answers.answer: With CHOAM, the contract icon lets you take one of the two face-up contracts and replace it with a face-up contract from the bank. If all contracts have been taken, it instead gives 2 Solari. Harvest completes when you send an Agent to a Maker space and gain the contract's specified spice amount that turn in total; Immediate completes as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow completes when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: Taking contracts; Completing contracts: Harvest, Immediate, Acquire The Spice Must Flow.

answers.answer: No. If you take a board-space contract after already placing your Agent at that space this turn, you must wait for a future turn; you must hold it when sending the Agent. On completion, announce it, gain its shown rewards, then flip it face down and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: Completing contracts: already-visited space must wait; FAQ says announce, gain rewards, flip face down, leave in supply.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival as the third competitor. The Rival gets the Ornithopter Objective; the other two eligible Objectives are dealt randomly to humans, and the human whose Objective shows First Player gets the marker. First Player alternates only between humans. Each round order is First Player → Rival → other human. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and Agent turns.

answers.answer: For an occupied indicated destination, ignore it and reveal another House Hagal card. A Place Spy card does not place an Agent: try an empty post of the specified type, ignore placement if none exists, and immediately reveal another card either way. Ignore normal destination costs and effects; apply only the revealed Hagal effects. If Hagal empties or Reshuffle appears, immediately reshuffle and continue.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns; Place Spy cards; ignore normal space costs/effects; empty deck/Reshuffle procedure.

answers.answer: Shuffle Objective cards after removing those whose 1–3P/4/6P marking does not match the player count; distribute one eligible card face up to each player. The marked Objective identifies First Player. Shaddam may be used only with the CHOAM Module, so he cannot be chosen without it.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 3 and 5: Shaddam only with CHOAM; omit mismatched Objectives, distribute face up, marked Objective determines First Player.

answers.answer: The bank resources and sandworms are not limited; if they run out, make any convenient substitution. If your personal troop supply runs out, you cannot recruit more until troops return there. Gain Solari, spice, and water from the bank; payments of those resources go back to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: substitutions if bank runs out; resources taken from/returned to bank. Recruit section: empty troop supply prevents recruitment.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict and place it face up on top of any unclaimed earlier Conflict cards, resolve control's defensive troop bonus, then each player draws five cards. At Recall, if no Endgame, return Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start another round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phases; Round Start and Recall descriptions.

answers.answer: Yes. After paying costs and meeting requirements, you may resolve board-space and Agent-box effects in any order, and advance Influence for the Faction space. No: entry costs and requirements must be met before effects of the space or played card, so the visit's Influence cannot satisfy its own entry requirement.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements before effects; effects may be carried out in any order.

answers.answer: No. An arrow cost and its effect can be used only once per turn, even if you have enough resources to repeat it; sandworm reward doubling on a Conflict reward is the exception. Most card and space effects are mandatory; exceptions include “may,” optional arrow costs, and the black-X trash icon. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ—Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from your supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have no Spies in supply, you may first recall one of your own Spies for no effect. If the placement effect requires a particular Agent-icon type connected to that post, you must satisfy it or cannot place there.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: unoccupied post; may recall if supply empty; specified Agent icon constraint.

answers.answer: No. Infiltrate bypasses another player's Agent only, not your own. You still must play a card for an Agent turn; recalling a Spy does not itself send an Agent. You cannot recall two Spies to Gather Intelligence twice on the same placement; you may use one for Infiltrate and another for Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts; FAQ—Spies: recall requires card, two different effects allowed, never two Gather Intelligence.

answers.answer: When a player visits a controlled critical location, the controller gets the location's bonus even if the controller is the visitor: Arrakeen or Spice Refinery gives 1 Solari, Imperial Basin gives 1 spice. Winning its named Conflict places your Control marker, replacing an opponent's. When its Conflict is revealed, its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Critical Locations & Control; board-space table separates visitor and controller effects; Round Start defensive bonus.

answers.answer: In a three-player tie for second, each tied player gets the third reward; the winner keeps first reward and the Conflict card, and there are no further rewards. Players tied for third get nothing. If three players tie for first, each gets the second reward, nobody wins or takes the card, and nobody else gets a reward (in either three- or four-player play).
answers.evidence: Combat ties and player-count table.

answers.answer: With three players and three different positive strengths, first and second place receive rewards; third gets nothing. The same applies in two-player play with its Rival as third competitor: ordinary first and second receive rewards, ordinary third does not, except third reward is used for a tie for second.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: in 2 or 3 players ordinary first and second receive rewards, third does not; Rival included.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigues may be played during your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigues during Combat; Endgame Intrigues at game end. Keep unplayed Intrigues face down, separate from your deck; you may look at them, reveal only when played, and put resolved cards face up in a discard pile by the Intrigue Deck. If the Intrigue deck runs out, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Intrigue cards; FAQ—Draw timing: if Intrigue deck runs out, reshuffle discard.

answers.answer: An ordinary discard instruction cannot discard an Intrigue unless it specifies Intrigue; ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand. Secrets' separate steal effect takes one Intrigue at random from each opponent who has four or more Intrigues.
answers.evidence: Discarding; Intrigue cards: Steal Intrigue icon threshold and random selection.

answers.answer: Trashing can remove cards from your hand, discard pile, or in play; return ordinary trashed cards to the box and Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it pays a cost or the card says to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove its acquire VP; that VP is retained.
answers.evidence: Trashing section; FAQ—Victory: Spice Must Flow acquire VP retained if later trashed.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once at the moment you acquire the card. When you cannot draw because your deck is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. Unused Persuasion is lost at the end of your Reveal turn and cannot be saved.
answers.evidence: Acquire box; Acquiring Cards; unused Persuasion lost.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and revealed during Reveal remain face up in play until Clean Up unless trashed first. Two Fremen Bond cards can activate one another regardless of the order played, provided each has another Fremen card in play. They cease being in play at Clean Up when moved to the discard pile.
answers.evidence: In play / Fremen Bond: other Fremen cards in play; reciprocal activation; Clean Up.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent you sent that turn; it can be used on another Agent turn in the same round. Retreat moves a troop from the Conflict to your garrison. “Retreat any number” permits zero.
answers.evidence: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ says retreat any number allows zero.

answers.answer: A free-choice gain of two Influence must go to one chosen Faction and cannot be split between two. Faction-specific icons apply only to their named Faction. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction's Alliance token; an effect with a minimum Influence requirement requires meeting the named minimum.
answers.evidence: Influence: free-choice gain two with one Faction; Alliance icon and minimum Influence requirements.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied, the formerly tied opponent takes the Alliance; if multiple opponents were tied, the former holder chooses which receives it. If the holder drops to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the Alliance to the board and the former holder loses its 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Victory Points—Faction Influence; FAQ—Alliance loss.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is revealed immediately and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the five cards then drawn. A Plot Intrigue played earlier that has a later Reveal effect remains face up until that effect is used, then is discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Combat and troops: win-trigger Intrigues cannot follow a first-place tie; if received as winning reward may be played immediately.

answers.answer: If final VP and all four listed resource tiebreakers remain tied, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed the printed 12-space track.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Victory.

answers.answer: No. All contracts held for the same space must be fulfilled with one Agent placement, and the contract must be held when sending the Agent. A board-space contract is another effect of that Agent turn and can resolve in any order with the space and Agent-box effects.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Contract completion is mandatory.

answers.answer: Shaddam does not start with the set-aside Sardaukar contracts. When acquiring a contract, Sardaukar Commander lets him choose one of those instead of a generally available one. Emperor of the Known Universe applies immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send an Agent, and restricts deployment for that turn only, not the whole round.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Shaddam.

answers.answer: Feyd's token starts on the leftmost space of his Leader's Training track and stays at the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins with her Lady Jessica side face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications; FAQ says Reverend Mother Jessica may act on flip turn.

answers.answer: For Margot and Irulan, moving from 1 to 3 reaches 2 even when gaining multiple Influence at once. They can reach 2 again later by losing Influence and regaining it upward; moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild's Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications: Margot/Irulan and Spacing Guild's Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses the Spice Trade icon and always draws one card; with CHOAM it also takes a contract, and without CHOAM or when none remain it gives 2 Solari instead. Dutiful Service uses the Emperor icon, gives 1 Emperor Influence, and likewise takes a contract with CHOAM or gives 2 Solari without/no contracts. Neither space automatically gains Faction Influence from its access icon; Accept Contract gives no automatic Influence, while Dutiful's listed 1 Emperor Influence is an explicit effect.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide preface and Accept Contract/Dutiful Service rows.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while controller gets 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw a card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert costs 3 water, base choice 4 spice or (with Hooks) two sandworms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water, base choice 2 spice or (with Hooks) one sandworm. Both also give all bonus spice present, including when choosing worms. Hooks are retained and not spent when summoning. Protected Conflicts at Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, and Imperial Basin cannot receive a worm while the Shield Wall remains.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows; Makers; Sandworms/FAQ Hooks retained and Shield Wall.

answers.answer: Both Sietch Tabr options require City access and 2+ Fremen Influence, with no resource entry cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if you lack them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option does not grant a troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr options and requirements.

answers.answer: High Council is Landsraad, not a Combat space. Each visit costs 5 Solari. On the first visit, place your Councilor on an unoccupied seat and gain 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. On subsequent visits, gain 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council row.

answers.answer: Swordmaster costs 8 Solari before anyone has one and 6 Solari after anyone has one; each player may take it only once per game. Take your third Agent from beside the board onto your Leader; it is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival obtaining its Swordmaster also reduces human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster row.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege is Landsraad and requires 2+ Emperor Influence plus 3 Solari entry cost. Its effects let you discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue, then recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It does not automatically give Emperor Influence, and it recalls another Agent, not the one just placed.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege row; Recall Agent rule.

answers.answer: Shipping uses Spice Trade access, requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence, and costs 3 spice. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; that Influence need not be Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping row.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad, not Combat; choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari. It recruits two troops either way, and paying 2 also gains 1 water. Spice Refinery is City and Combat yes; choose 0 or 1 spice, gaining 2 Solari or 4 Solari if you pay 1 spice; its controller separately gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild, Combat yes, costs 5 spice; gains 1 Guild Influence and recruits five troops. Desert Tactics: Fremen, Combat yes, costs 1 water; gains 1 Fremen Influence, recruits one troop, and may trash a card. Sardaukar: Emperor, Combat no, costs 4 spice; gains 1 Emperor Influence, draws an Intrigue, and recruits four troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall is Landsraad, no cost, not Combat: draw an Intrigue, and if your Agent is there gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal turn. Espionage is Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, not Combat: gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies is Spacing Guild, no cost, not Combat: gain 1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide rows Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: False Orders makes affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent's destination that turn; it may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Litany Against Fear's red box is ignored during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played normally as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Leader/card rulings: False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the card removed by Manipulate. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If no one acquires it by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ—Manipulate.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four Influence cubes at track bottoms, three troops in garrison and the others in supply, two Agents in supply with Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, and 1 water; score and Combat marker are 0. Shuffle House Hagal and retain its 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival is a scoring competitor and its 10+ VP triggers Endgame at Recall; it can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules—Setup and Rival scoring.

answers.answer: As soon as its total of Solari, spice, Intrigue cards and water reaches the printed Swordmaster threshold, the Rival spends that many and takes its third Agent, usable this round. It counts each unit/card as one. Spend Solari first, then spice, then Intrigue cards, then water; keep leftovers. The third Agent is immediately usable in the current round.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, it spends each set of 7 Solari for 1 VP, 7 spice for 1 VP, 3 Intrigue cards for 1 VP, or 3 water for 1 VP. It cannot make a mixed set of seven resources for a VP; the stated VP exchanges are separate exact resource sets.
answers.evidence: Rival Resources and Swordmaster: exact sets and VP.

answers.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence and breaks ties by leftmost priority icon. It gets the 2-Influence VP and Alliance token VP like a human, but not the resource/track bonus for reaching 4 Influence. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that numbered position in its Faction-priority list.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat and Resources: Influence choice; Influence VP/Alliance; no 4 track resource bonus. Hagal numbered Influence definition.

answers.answer: No. With a two-destination card, choose only the destination matching current conditions; if it is occupied, reveal another card and do not use the other destination. Accept Contract/Shipping selection depends on Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies/Heighliner depends on Conflict tier.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: two-destination conditions and occupied destination rule.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruited none. Troops recruited at a noncombat space go to its garrison. A conditional bonus at 2+ Influence is simply omitted if unmet; that does not prevent the Agent placement.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: troop icons and Combat spaces; conditional bonus does not prevent placement.

answers.answer: Unless a post type is specified, the Rival puts a Spy at the first available Faction observation post in its priority order; if all four are occupied, ignore placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls its other two and triggers its printed Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If its Scheme recruits troops before placement and the Rival reaches a Combat space that turn, deploy those Scheme-recruited troops too. If a Place Spy card has no legal empty post, ignore its placement and immediately reveal another Hagal card because it did not send an Agent.
answers.evidence: Rival Spies and Schemes; Place Spy cards do not place an Agent.

answers.answer: The Rival always collects accumulated bonus spice at a visited Maker space. At Hagga Basin or Deep Desert, with Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, it summons one or two worms respectively instead of base spice. Without Hooks, or when the Conflict is protected, it summons none and takes the base spice (Hagga 2; Deep Desert 4). Bonus spice is still collected in addition to that choice.
answers.evidence: Rival Maker spaces; Sandworm limitations; bonus spice collected.

answers.answer: At the start of Combat, if the Rival has at least one unit deployed, reveal one Hagal card in turn order and add only its bottom swords to strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Humans then have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A unit-free Rival does not get this bonus.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat.

answers.answer: Yes: Rival receives normal placement rewards, may double rewards with worms, wins Conflict cards and battle-icon VP normally, gets control bonuses on visits, and gets a defensive troop from supply when its controlled Conflict is revealed. It takes an optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat; Rival never takes contracts.

answers.answer: During Resolve Reveal Effects, total and announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point; update it as needed while resolving the Reveal turn. If strength exceeds 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn; Strength section.

answers.answer: A Leader's Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on one of your Agent turns; merely revealing that card does not activate it. Cards of any type can override the usual rules of the game.
answers.evidence: Setup Leader abilities; Overview: cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a powerful effect. It is not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate effects available by recalling a connected Spy when sending an Agent.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: Recall Spy icon and distinct Infiltrate/Gather Intelligence effects.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction discards a non-Intrigue card of your choice from your hand unless it specifies otherwise; it does not trash the card.
answers.evidence: Trashing; Discarding.

answers.answer: If a Conflict reward gives one free-choice Influence and a sandworm doubles the reward, the two Influence gains may be assigned to the same Faction or to two different Factions. That is distinct from a single icon/effect granting two free-choice Influence, which must all go to one Faction.
answers.evidence: Sandworm Reward Doubling example; Influence free-choice rule.

answers.answer: Resolve the Rival card's printed Signet Ring ability. It is a Hagal effect, so the Rival does not need a human Signet Ring card or a Reveal turn; Rivals take Agent turns using Hagal cards and never Reveal.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns apply printed Signet Ring effects; Rival never Reveals.

answers.answer: A Maker Hooks icon gives the Rival a token from the bank if it does not already have one; if it already has Hooks, it takes no second token. A Shield Wall removal effect removes the Wall only if the Rival has Hooks and the Wall remains. Without Hooks it is ignored, and an already removed Wall has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Rival Hooks and Wall icons table.

answers.answer: Secrets uses Bene Gesserit access, costs nothing, and is not a Combat space. It gives 1 Bene Gesserit Influence and draws an Intrigue from the Intrigue Deck; separately, each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives you one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Secrets row.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin uses Spice Trade access, has no cost, and is a Combat space. The visitor gains 1 base spice plus all bonus spice there. The controller separately gets 1 spice; if visitor and controller are the same player, that player gets both effects.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Basin row; controller and visitor effects both resolve.

answers.answer: Place the newly revealed Conflict face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards left from earlier rounds. Resolve the defensive troop bonus for a controlled location, then each player draws five cards; thus Conflict is revealed before the round's hand is drawn.
answers.evidence: Phase 1 Round Start.

answers.answer: Place one human cube at the bottom of each of the four Faction Influence tracks. Put the four Alliance tokens on their marked track areas; no human starts holding one. The Shield Wall token begins in its marked area below Spice Refinery, so it is present.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 6; normal setup assigns no Maker Hooks, but Alliance tokens start on tracks.

answers.answer: The First Player takes the first turn, then play proceeds clockwise. A player who Reveals is skipped for the rest of Player Turns; in 3–4 players the phase ends once all players have Revealed. In Combat Intrigue, priority starts with First Player and goes clockwise. Each eligible player may play any number of Combat Intrigues or pass; the window resolves once all involved pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Player Turns and Combat Intrigue procedures.

answers.answer: The three Reveal steps are: Reveal Cards (reveal all remaining hand cards); Resolve Reveal Effects (resolve their Reveal boxes, in any order, use Persuasion/acquire and set strength); Clean Up (move all cards in front of you to discard). The effects need not follow card order; the player may choose their order.
answers.evidence: Reveal Turn: three steps; effects resolved in any order.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human's 10-card starting deck and place it face down in their supply. Without CHOAM, omit CHOAM-marked cards, shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks separately face down, deal five face-up Imperium cards as the Row, and place Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Human Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies start in supply; Councilor starts with the player components in supply, and Control markers start in supply.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 4 and 6; Initial card states; player components list.

answers.answer: During a Reveal turn, ordinary Persuasion acquires any of the five Imperium Row cards or Prepare the Way/The Spice Must Flow from the Reserve. The cost is at the top right of the card. These ordinary Persuasion purchases occur during Reveal, not Agent turns.
answers.evidence: Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional, even when legal; declining a recall used as a cost also declines the associated benefit, and an Intrigue still requires all its costs. Shield Wall removal is optional (“may remove”). Once removed, it is gone for the rest of the game and cannot return in a later round.
answers.evidence: Spies & observation posts: placement/recall optional; Shield Wall: may remove, gone rest of game.

answers.answer: The played card must have a matching Agent icon for the destination; you choose one icon and the destination must be unoccupied unless Infiltrate applies. A Spy connected to Shipping does not let a City-only card send an Agent there. If the played card actually has a Spy Agent icon, it can send an Agent to any board space connected to your Spy's post, without recalling that Spy.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn and Spy Agent icon rules.

answers.answer: Yes. During your Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue; resources it grants before entry are available to pay that destination cost. Resources from the card you play to send the Agent or from the destination are gained only after placement and cannot pay that same entry cost.
answers.evidence: Player Turns entry-cost timing.

answers.answer: No. Even if both humans have Revealed, continue the Rival's Agent turns while it has Agents in supply. Proceed to Combat only after both humans have Revealed and the Rival has used all its Agents. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: two-player Rival timing.

answers.answer: When the Conflict card for a location you already control is revealed at Round Start, its controller may deploy one troop from supply directly to the Conflict; it is optional and requires no Agent visit. After Combat rewards, return each player's Conflict troops to supply, reset all Combat markers to 0, and return sandworms to the bank.
answers.evidence: Phase 1 Round Start; Resolve Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to an unoccupied matching space. Resolve the played card's Agent box and ignore its Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or discard pile, or move an Agent already on the board; the Agent turn uses a card from hand and an Agent from your Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: play one card from hand; send Agent from Leader; card remains in front; use Agent box.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when Shaddam plays Signet Ring to send the Agent; he cannot delay it by resolving the board space first. The Leader clarification says this restriction on deploying units takes effect immediately on that Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Leader clarifications—Shaddam Corrino IV.

answers.answer: In four-player play, first, second, and third place receive the corresponding printed rewards; fourth place receives no reward. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card face up, then checks battle-icon matches.
answers.evidence: Resolve Combat: four-player ordinary ranks; winner takes Conflict card.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random; random distribution is not required.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3: each player takes a Leader (choose, or select at random).

answers.answer: An ordinary draw-a-card effect draws from your own deck. You may not choose a card directly from your discard pile; if your deck is empty, shuffle the discard pile into a new deck and draw from it.
answers.evidence: Drawing cards.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the shared Rival; retain the 2P Reshuffle card. When the deck empties or Reshuffle appears during play, reshuffle immediately and continue.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules setup and Agent turns.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. When acquired, a token moves from the bank onto that player's garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: all Maker Hooks in common bank; later acquired token goes to garrison.

answers.answer: Yes. If a Combat Intrigue changes deployed units or otherwise changes strength, adjust the participant's Combat marker when that card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. The Reveal-turn total is not fixed; Combat rewards use the adjusted strength shown on the track when Combat resolves.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: adjust marker when card resolves; use adjusted strength.

answers.answer: Gained Solari, spice, and water come from the bank. You do not take them from another player's supply; resource payments return to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7: resources gained from bank, paid resources returned to bank.

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contracts face down first. Then flip two face up for the board offers and place the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Players do not choose the two offers or preset the face-down order; the contracts are shuffled before the offers are exposed.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Setup changes: shuffle 20 face down, flip two face up, remaining 18 face down in bank.
